keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «인플레이션은 물건과 서비스 가격이 전반적으로 올라 같은 돈으로 전보다 덜 사게 되는 것이다(개념)» 와 «물가를 잡기 위해 한국은행 같은 중앙은행은 금리를 올릴 수 있다(해결책)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the concept (inflation is a general increase in prices, so the same money buys less) and the solution (central banks such as the Bank of Korea can raise interest rates to control it). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: What inflation is and why it happens
People want to buy more than the economy makes, and the costs of making things rise
Central banks raise interest rates so people spend less

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

qs.q: Why can high inflation make life hard for families?
qs.qko: 높은 인플레이션은 왜 가족들의 생활을 힘들게 할 수 있나요?
opts: Prices rise faster than wages, and savings lose value
Central banks take away their savings
Prices fall so fast that stores close
evs: When prices rise faster than wages, families find it harder to pay for basic needs, and savings lose value.
A small amount of inflation, around 2 percent a year, is considered healthy by many central banks.
Surprisingly, falling prices, or deflation, can also be harmful, because people may delay spending and the economy can slow down.
Economists usually measure it with a price index, which tracks the cost of a typical basket of goods such as food, rent, and transportation.
why: 본문에 가격이 월급보다 빨리 오르면 가족들이 기본적인 필요를 감당하기 어려워지고 저축의 가치도 떨어진다고 나와요.
When prices rise faster than wages, families find it harder to pay for basic needs, and savings lose value.

qs.q: In the text, what does "a typical basket of goods" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «a typical basket of goods» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: A set of common things people usually buy, like food, rent, and transportation
A real shopping basket full of fruit
The money a bank keeps in a safe
evs: Economists usually measure it with a price index, which tracks the cost of a typical basket of goods such as food, rent, and transportation.
More precisely, inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services, which means that the same amount of money buys less than before.
Printing too much money can also lead to inflation.
Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, so people and businesses spend less, which helps cool prices.
why: 여기서 «basket» 은 진짜 바구니가 아니라 사람들이 흔히 사는 것들의 묶음을 말해요. 같은 문장에서 음식, 집세, 교통비 같은 예를 들어요.
Here "basket" is not a real basket. It means a set of things people usually buy, such as food, rent, and transportation.

qs.q: How can raising interest rates help cool prices?
qs.qko: 금리를 올리면 어떻게 물가를 식히는 데 도움이 되나요?
opts: Borrowing becomes more expensive, so people and businesses spend less
Banks print more money for everyone
Companies pass higher oil costs on to customers
evs: To control inflation, central banks such as the Bank of Korea can raise interest rates.
Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, so people and businesses spend less, which helps cool prices.
Printing too much money can also lead to inflation.
First, when people and businesses want to buy more than the economy can produce, prices are pulled up.
why: 중앙은행은 물가를 잡으려고 금리를 올리고, 금리가 오르면 돈을 빌리기가 비싸져서 사람과 기업이 덜 쓰게 돼요. 그래서 물가가 식어요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
Central banks raise interest rates to control inflation. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, so people and businesses spend less, which cools prices.
